title: Geometric inverse image from the profinite point and its monoidal comparisons
statement:
Choose universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathbf{Prof}$ be the category of compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces and continuous maps in the smaller universe, equipped with the topology generated by finite jointly surjective families. Use sheaves valued in the larger universe. For a scheme $T$ use $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Set $a(S)=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, where $\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$ is the ring of locally constant integer-valued functions with pointwise operations; continuous maps act by precomposition and then contravariantly by spectrum. Then $a(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is weakly etale, $a$ preserves finite limits as a functor to the pro-etale site, and $a$ sends finite jointly surjective covering families to pro-etale coverings. Left Kan extension along $a^{op}$ followed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] exists with these universe conventions and defines the inverse image $a^*$ of a geometric morphism. Its abelian-sheaf functor is exact and strong symmetric monoidal for sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

For any scheme $T$ with structure morphism $\pi_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, put $p_T^*=\pi_T^{-1}a^*$ using [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For every scheme morphism $h:T\to U$, the inverse-image composition comparison and $\pi_Uh=\pi_T$ give a canonical monoidal natural isomorphism $h^{-1}p_U^*\cong p_T^*$. These comparisons are compatible with identity morphisms and composition. The corresponding composition comparisons for the abelian inverse images, their lifts to ring and module sheaves, and their termwise functors on derived categories are compatible with identity morphisms and composition. In particular the induced comparison for any commutative square is the one obtained by comparing each composite pullback with the pullback of the common composite scheme morphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor] with $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Its existence, weak-etaleness, presentation-independence and functorial-identification assertions identify its relative functor with the explicitly defined $a(S)=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$, including the maps induced by precomposition. Its finite-limit and cover assertions give exactly the required properties of $a$. Thus no inverse-limit or pro-etale construction is being treated as elementary.

source.place: Section 4 finite-XI, XS, lem:XS; Basic.lean module docstring 38–52

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] to $a$. The profinite site has a final singleton and fibre products of profinite spaces, hence finite limits; the lemma in step 1 gives their preservation and cover preservation. The small skeletons and larger sheaf universe are those in [def-weil-size-convention] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The theorem supplies existence of the left Kan extension, the sheafified adjunction, left exactness and preservation of all colimits, and the exact strong symmetric monoidal abelian inverse image $a^*$. Apply the same theorem to the scheme base-change site functors of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] to obtain their corresponding exact tensor structures; their preservation of the final object, fibre products and coverings is part of that node's specified site functor.

For composable scheme morphisms $h:T\to U$, $k:U\to V$, the site functors compose through $(T\times_U(U\times_V W))\cong T\times_VW$. This is the canonical fibre-product associativity map: it preserves the maps to $T$ and $W$, and its inverse is the unique map with these projections. Consequently all its associativity and identity diagrams commute by uniqueness of maps to fibre products. Use [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] to obtain the adjunction-compatible inverse-image comparison $c_{k,h}:h^{-1}k^{-1}\cong(kh)^{-1}$ (on sets and abelian sheaves). To apply [lem-sc-left-adjoint-composition-iso-associativity], whose statement assumes equal right adjoints, first use strictly composed right adjoints along the chain: let $R_{ji}$ be the ordered composite of the individual direct images from vertex $j$ to vertex $i$, so $R_{ki}=R_{ji}R_{kj}$, and take the composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Transport the single-morphism inverse-image adjunction to these right adjoints using the fibre-product comparison above. The unique transport and comparison isomorphisms are those of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. The associativity lemma now applies with the actual equalities $R_{ki}=R_{ji}R_{kj}$. Returning through the transports identifies its $c$ with the original adjunction-compatible comparisons by the unit equation. This proves their associativity without applying an equality-only lemma to unequal direct-image functors. For an identity, compare with the identity adjunction: both candidate maps carry the unit to the same unit and hence agree by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. These are monoidal comparisons by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor].

proof.text: Write $\pi_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ for the structure morphism. Define $p_T^*=\pi_T^{-1}a^*$. For $h:T\to U$ the equality $\pi_Uh=\pi_T$ identifies $c_{\pi_U,h}a^*$ with an isomorphism $\alpha_h:h^{-1}p_U^*\cong p_T^*$. Naturality follows from naturality of $c$ and whiskering by $a^*$; monoidality follows from step 3. This is the source comparison defined in the exact master by inverse-image composition and the structure-map identity.

source.place: Section 5 basechange-XS, triangle, thm:alpha; exact master Basic.lean 61–71

proof.text: For $h:T\to U$ and $k:U\to V$, associativity of $c$ applied to $h,k,\pi_V$ says $\alpha_{kh}\circ(c_{k,h}p_V^*)=\alpha_h\circ h^{-1}\alpha_k$. For $h=\mathrm{id}$ the unit equation for $c$ gives the identity comparison for $p_T^*$. Applying $\alpha_h$ to a condensed ring $\Lambda$ gives a ring isomorphism: the lift of inverse image to group and ring objects is [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-group-ring-objects], interpreted as ring sheaves via [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]. Naturality with respect to addition, negation, zero, multiplication and one ensures the component preserves each operation. Thus, with $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, the ring coefficient map $\theta_h:h^{-1}R_U\cong R_T$ satisfies precisely the displayed composite equation.

source.place: Section 5 thm:alpha and composition coherence; sites.tex 00YV

proof.text: For a fixed condensed commutative ring $\Lambda$, set $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and use the invertible coefficient maps of step 5. Define the action on $h^{-1}M$ by applying the finite-product-preserving inverse image to the action on $M$ and then substituting $\theta_h^{-1}$ in the scalar variable; all module equations follow by applying this functor to the equations defining a module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The extension-of-scalars identification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is explicitly $R_T\otimes_{h^{-1}R_U}h^{-1}M\to h^{-1}M$, $r\otimes m\mapsto\theta_h^{-1}(r)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$; the balancing relation proves these are inverse, and they pass through sheafification. Thus module pullback has the exact underlying abelian functor of step 2; kernels and sheafified cokernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] give module exactness. For composition, naturality at the action map says $c_M\circ h^{-1}k^{-1}\mu=(kh)^{-1}\mu\circ(c_{R_V}\times c_M)$ under the canonical product identifications. Substitution of $\theta_{kh}=\theta_h\circ h^{-1}\theta_k\circ c_{k,h,R_V}^{-1}$ makes this precisely $R_T$-linearity. The abelian unit and associativity equations of step 3 are consequently equations of module maps, since forgetting the action is faithful. This is the direct few-line action and tensor calculation of Stacks 03D2 and 03D8 with invertible coefficients; it needs no separate lemma.

source.place: sites-modules.tex Tags 03D2, 03D3, 03D8; exact master Basic.lean coefficient/module construction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to each exact abelian or coefficient-preserving module pullback above. Its termwise complex functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to the unbounded derived category without resolutions. For each sheaf-level comparison $c$, naturality at a differential $d^r$ gives $c_{M^{r+1}}L_1(d^r)=L_2(d^r)c_{M^r}$, so its components form an isomorphism of complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2), this comparison and its inverse descend uniquely to a derived natural isomorphism. That clause respects identities and composition, and clause (3) detects equality after localization; therefore the degreewise unit and associativity equations descend to the derived comparisons. This separately proves the derived coherence, rather than inferring it from a ring-sheaf component.

proof.text: For a commutative square $T'\xrightarrow{b}T\xrightarrow{f}U$ and $T'\xrightarrow{f'}U'\xrightarrow{g}U$ with $fb=gf'=r$, compare $b^{-1}f^{-1}$ and $f'^{-1}g^{-1}$ by $c_{g,f'}^{-1}c_{f,b}$, both of whose middle targets are $r^{-1}$. For the coefficient pullbacks, step 5 makes both routes to $p_{T'}^*$ equal to $\alpha_r$. The module comparison of step 6 is the same map on underlying abelian sheaves, so the square equality remains true after its linear lift. Step 7 preserves this equation under localization. This gives exactly the stipulated commutative-square comparison in all coefficient categories.
